current_law_statement: Reviewed 2024, 2025 and 2026 legislative sessions for the fee sections. Primary source: owner-supplied official 2025 Minnesota Statutes text of Minn. Stat. § 13.03 (revisor.mn.gov, history through '2025 c 35 art 5 s 1; art 9 s 1'), which includes the NEW 2025 subd. 3(g) five-business-day collection/suspension rule (2025 c 35) — the known recency gap, captured here as rule MN-9001. Minn. Stat. § 13.04 checked online at revisor.mn.gov: current through 2026 c 95 art 1 s 2, which amended only subd. 4a (sex-offender-program data challenge procedure, no fee content); the subd. 3 data-subject fee sentence is unchanged. Delegated instruments Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4 and 1205.0400 subp. 5 opened at revisor.mn.gov (published electronically July 13, 2007; statutory authority Minn. Stat. § 13.07) — they contain reasonable-fee factors, no dollar figures. MN Dept. of Administration Data Practices Office 'Copy Costs' and 'Actual Cost' pages (owner-supplied, fetched 2026-08-20) are OFFICIAL GUIDANCE (Commissioner advisory-opinion layer), not statute; they are consistent with the statute except two guidance-only glosses: the 50-cents-per-two-sided-page figure and the 'flat rate — no add-on charges' reading of the 25-cent path, both flagged. No 2026 session law amending the § 13.03 fee provisions was found. Chapter 13 applies to all 'government entities' (state agencies, statewide systems, and political subdivisions), so its fee rules bind municipalities directly; § 13.03 subd. 10 (deposit of collected copy money) is state-agency accounting only.

resolutions.unit: USD per page (100 or fewer black-and-white letter/legal-size paper pages; above 100 pages the basis reverts to actual cost)
resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(c)
resolutions.source_language: However, if 100 or fewer pages of black and white, letter or legal size paper copies are requested, actual costs shall not be used, and instead, the responsible authority may charge no more than 25 cents for each page copied.
resolutions.notes: Ceiling, not a fixed rate — 'may charge no more than'. Applies to all government entities including municipalities. DPO guidance (MN-9009) adds two guidance-only glosses: 50 cents for a two-sided copy, and that the 25-cent charge is a flat rate with no add-ons (no mailing/paper surcharge). Above 100 pages: actual cost (see rules.maxFee).

resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(c)
resolutions.source_language: If a person requests copies or electronic transmittal of the data to the person, the responsible authority may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of searching for and retrieving government data, including the cost of employee time, and for making, certifying, and electronically transmitting the copies of the data or the data, but may not charge for separating public from not public data.
resolutions.notes: The 25-cent path is expressly limited to 'black and white, letter or legal size paper copies' — the prior's value_present status was WRONG for color. Color copies fall to the actual-cost standard ('actual costs'). DPO guidance confirms: 'For copies of other data ... government may charge the actual cost.'

resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(c)
resolutions.source_language: If a person requests copies or electronic transmittal of the data to the person, the responsible authority may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of searching for and retrieving government data, including the cost of employee time, and for making, certifying, and electronically transmitting the copies of the data or the data, but may not charge for separating public from not public data.
resolutions.notes: The 25-cent path is limited to 'letter or legal size' paper; oversized/nonstandard pages fall to the actual-cost standard. No separate oversized rate anywhere in ch. 13, Minn. R. 1205, or DPO guidance.

resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(c); MN Dept. of Administration DPO, 'Actual Cost' (Advisory Opinions 95-044, 97-012)
resolutions.source_language: If a person requests copies or electronic transmittal of the data to the person, the responsible authority may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of searching for and retrieving government data, including the cost of employee time, and for making, certifying, and electronically transmitting the copies of the data or the data, but may not charge for separating public from not public data.
resolutions.notes: Specialty reproduction (photographs etc.) is actual cost; DPO guidance confirms 'Costs of reproduction that cannot be done by the entity, such as photographs' are includable in actual cost (Advisory Opinions 95-044, 97-012). No fixed specialty schedule exists at the state level.

resolutions.value: band 1: <=100 pages b/w letter/legal paper -> ceiling $0.25/page (actual cost prohibited); band 2: all other copies -> actual cost
resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(c)
resolutions.source_language: However, if 100 or fewer pages of black and white, letter or legal size paper copies are requested, actual costs shall not be used, and instead, the responsible authority may charge no more than 25 cents for each page copied.
resolutions.notes: The state itself creates a two-band structure the engine must execute: the 100-page boundary switches the basis (25-cent ceiling below, actual cost above), it does not merely change a rate. On the <=100-page band actual costs 'shall not be used' — a prohibition, so search/retrieval labor is not chargeable on that band.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04; Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO Copy Costs / Actual Cost guidance
resolutions.notes: No free-page allowance found in ch. 13, the ch. 1205 rules, or DPO guidance — chargeable from page 1. Charging is permissive ('The Data Practices Act allows, but does not require, government to charge for copies'), so a city MAY adopt a free-page allowance by local policy; the state does not require one. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(c); MN Dept. of Administration DPO, 'Actual Cost' (Advisory Opinion 04-056)
resolutions.source_language: If a person requests copies or electronic transmittal of the data to the person, the responsible authority may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of searching for and retrieving government data, including the cost of employee time, and for making, certifying, and electronically transmitting the copies of the data or the data, but may not charge for separating public from not public data.
resolutions.notes: No fixed $/hr rate. Guidance layer (MN-9008): 'Employee time must be calculated based on the wages/salary (may include benefits) of the lowest-paid entity employee who could complete the task' (Advisory Opinion 04-056). Not chargeable: on the <=100-page b/w flat-rate band; for inspection-only requests; for search/retrieval when the requester is the data subject.

resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(c)
resolutions.source_language: ... but may not charge for separating public from not public data.
resolutions.notes: Review/redaction labor is categorically non-chargeable in Minnesota — the statute prohibits charging 'for separating public from not public data', so a review/redaction rate cannot exist. DPO guidance confirms (Advisory Opinion 04-072: employee time to separate public from not public data cannot be included; 'Government may not charge any fee for redaction or separation of public data from not public data').

resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(e)
resolutions.source_language: The entity may require the requesting person to pay the actual cost of providing the copy.
resolutions.notes: No fixed programming/extraction rate. Electronic copies from a computer storage medium are chargeable at 'the actual cost of providing the copy' (subd. 3(e)); the entity is NOT required to provide data in a different format or program than the one it maintains, so bespoke conversion/programming is not compellable. Employee-time rate per guidance: lowest-paid employee who could complete the task (MN-9008).

resolutions.value: labor chargeable ONLY when copies or electronic transmittal are requested; NEVER for inspection-only; NEVER on the <=100-page b/w letter/legal flat-rate band (actual costs prohibited there); NEVER for separating public from not public data; search/retrieval time NEVER chargeable to a data-subject requester
resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(a), (c); § 13.04, subd. 3
resolutions.source_language: If a person requests access for the purpose of inspection, the responsible authority may not assess a charge or require the requesting person to pay a fee to inspect data. [subd. 3(a)] ... If a person requests copies or electronic transmittal of the data to the person, the responsible authority may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of searching for and retrieving government data, including the cost of employee time ... but may not charge for separating public from not public data. However, if 100 or fewer pages of black and white, letter or legal size paper copies are requested, actual costs shall not be used ... [subd. 3(c)]
resolutions.notes: No page/hour threshold gates labor — the gate is the request TYPE (copies vs inspection) and the band (flat-rate band excludes actual costs). Data-subject carve-out from DPO guidance: 'Entities cannot charge for search and retrieval time when the requestor is the data subject' (per § 13.04 subd. 3, which allows only making-and-certifying costs).

resolutions.source_authority: MN Dept. of Administration DPO, 'Actual Cost' (Advisory Opinions 04-056, 01-066, 04-040)
resolutions.source_language: Note: Employee time must be calculated based on the wages/salary (may include benefits) of the lowest-paid entity employee who could complete the task (Advisory Opinion 04-056)
resolutions.manual_verification: Guidance layer only — no statutory or rule text sets or forbids a percentage; the advisory-opinion framework is the operative authority. Verify Advisory Opinions 04-056, 01-066, 04-040 if a city wants to include benefits.
resolutions.notes: No percentage surcharge is authorized. Actual benefits MAY be included in the employee-time wage base ('may include benefits'), but overhead is excluded: 'Operating expenses of copier, such as electricity, wear and tear, etc.' cannot be included (Advisory Opinions 01-066, 04-040), nor can invoice preparation, accounting functions, or sales tax. Engine value: no overhead %; benefits at actual cost only, folded into the hourly wage, not a multiplier.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04; Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO Copy Costs / Actual Cost guidance
resolutions.notes: No time increment or rounding rule found in statute, rules, or DPO guidance. City sets its own increment consistent with the actual-cost standard. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04; Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO Copy Costs / Actual Cost guidance
resolutions.notes: No free-labor-hours allowance per request found. Note the categorical exclusions instead (not hour-based): redaction labor never chargeable; search/retrieval never chargeable to data subjects; no labor at all on the <=100-page b/w flat-rate band. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. ch. 13 (§§ 13.03, 13.04 opened in full); Minn. R. ch. 1205; DPO guidance
resolutions.notes: No TX § 552.275-style per-requestor periodic free personnel time provision exists in the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, its rules, or DPO guidance. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04; Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO Copy Costs / Actual Cost guidance
resolutions.notes: No statutory or rule requirement to provide an itemized estimate or cost notice at any threshold. Subd. 3(d) (commercial-value data) contains the only documentation duty: on request, the entity 'shall provide sufficient documentation to explain and justify the fee being charged' — a justification duty after charging, not an estimate threshold. DPO Model Access Policies mention copy-cost language but are templates, not law. City sets its own estimate policy.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04; Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO guidance
resolutions.notes: No estimate-response window exists (no estimate requirement at all). The ADJACENT 2025 rule is different in kind: once data/copies are noticed as AVAILABLE, subd. 3(g) gives a 5-business-day inspect/collect window before the entity may suspend further response (MN-9001) — that is a post-production collection window, not an estimate-response window. Do not conflate.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04; Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO guidance
resolutions.notes: No revised-estimate trigger found (no estimate regime exists in Minnesota law). Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04; Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO guidance
resolutions.notes: No estimate-validity period found (no estimate regime exists in Minnesota law). Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04; Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO Copy Costs / Actual Cost guidance
resolutions.manual_verification: Several state-agency data-practices policies state that payment may be required in advance for large fees, resting on DPO advisory-opinion practice; the underlying opinions were not opened in this pass. If a city wants a prepayment/deposit threshold, verify against the DPO advisory-opinion library before relying on it.
resolutions.notes: No statutory or rule deposit/prepayment threshold exists. The statute's only payment gate is post-production: subd. 3(g) lets the entity suspend further response until produced copies are collected AND PAID FOR (MN-9001). Agency policy statements referencing advance payment are agency-specific practice, not municipal authority.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04; Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO guidance
resolutions.notes: No deposit-cap percentage exists (no statutory deposit regime at all). Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

resolutions.value: pay-on-collection gate: after notice that copies are available, the entity may suspend ALL further response to the request until the requester collects and pays for the copies produced
resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(g) (added by 2025 c 35)
resolutions.source_language: If a responsible authority has notified the requesting person that responsive data or copies are available for inspection or collection, and the requesting person does not inspect the data or collect the copies within five business days of the notification, the responsible authority may suspend any further response to the request until the requesting person inspects the data that has been made available, or collects and pays for the copies that have been produced.
resolutions.notes: The 2025 amendment makes payment-for-produced-copies an express condition of continued processing ('collects and pays for the copies that have been produced'). No express statutory authority for a pay-BEFORE-copying gate for the general public; agency practice asserting advance payment rests on unopened advisory opinions (see rules.deposit.threshold).

resolutions.unit: business days from availability notification; consequence = entity may suspend any further response to the request (not withdrawal) until inspection or collection-and-payment
resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(g) (added by 2025 c 35)
resolutions.source_language: If a responsible authority has notified the requesting person that responsive data or copies are available for inspection or collection, and the requesting person does not inspect the data or collect the copies within five business days of the notification, the responsible authority may suspend any further response to the request until the requesting person inspects the data that has been made available, or collects and pays for the copies that have been produced.
resolutions.notes: This is the known recency gap, now captured. Consequence is SUSPENSION (resumable on inspection or collection+payment), not deemed withdrawal, and it is permissive ('may suspend'). No prior-debt prepayment rule found. This was absent from the pre-2025 corpus.

resolutions.value: no deposit regime exists; nearest statutory clock effect is subd. 3(g): response clock may be suspended after 5 business days when produced copies are uncollected/unpaid; resumes on inspection or collection-and-payment
resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(g) (added by 2025 c 35)
resolutions.source_language: If a responsible authority has notified the requesting person that responsive data or copies are available for inspection or collection, and the requesting person does not inspect the data or collect the copies within five business days of the notification, the responsible authority may suspend any further response to the request until the requesting person inspects the data that has been made available, or collects and pays for the copies that have been produced.
resolutions.notes: Minnesota has no statutory deposit, so there is no deposit-clock rule as such; this row records the payment-linked clock effect that DOES exist. Grace = 5 business days from availability notice; lapse action = suspension of any further response; cure = inspection or collection+payment. Engine mapping: deposit_clock_effect n/a; use MN-9001 on the produced-copies path.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04; Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO guidance
resolutions.notes: No overrun/re-issue rules found — Minnesota has no estimate regime, so no revised-estimate requirement, collection block, or window restart exists. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.
out of scope per owner decision 2026-08-20 — finance-department policy, excluded from state rules profile

resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(c); Minn. R. 1205.0300, subp. 4
resolutions.source_language: If a person requests copies or electronic transmittal of the data to the person, the responsible authority may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of searching for and retrieving government data, including the cost of employee time, and for making, certifying, and electronically transmitting the copies of the data or the data, but may not charge for separating public from not public data.
resolutions.notes: The request-level ceiling IS the actual-cost standard ('actual costs' of search, retrieval, making, certifying, transmitting), refined by the delegated rule's reasonable-fee factors (Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4: materials, labor, standard schedule, machine-based special costs, mailing). On the <=100-page b/w band the cap is $0.25/page instead. Exception: subd. 3(d) commercial-value data may add a development-cost-related fee above copy costs (see 'commercial').

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04; Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO Copy Costs guidance
resolutions.notes: No de-minimis threshold found. Charging is entirely permissive ('The Data Practices Act allows, but does not require, government to charge for copies' — DPO guidance), so a city may adopt its own no-charge-below threshold. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04; Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO guidance
resolutions.notes: No minimum fee exists; the 25-cent figure is a per-page CEILING, not a minimum, and actual cost is a recovery ceiling. A minimum fee exceeding actual cost would conflict with the actual-cost standard. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(e); MN Dept. of Administration DPO, 'Actual Cost'
resolutions.source_language: The entity may require the requesting person to pay the actual cost of providing the copy.
resolutions.notes: No fixed CD/DVD/USB rate. Media cost is an actual-cost component — DPO guidance lists 'Cost of media (paper, USB flash drives, etc.)' as includable. Electronic copies chargeable at 'the actual cost of providing the copy' (subd. 3(e)).

resolutions.source_authority: Minn. R. 1205.0300, subp. 4(E); Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(a), (c)
resolutions.source_language: In determining the amount of the reasonable fee, the responsible authority shall be guided by the following: ... E. mailing costs.
resolutions.notes: Mailing at actual cost — an enumerated reasonable-fee factor in the delegated rule and an includable in DPO guidance ('Mailing costs'). EXCEPTION (guidance-only gloss, MN-9009): on the <=100-page b/w flat-rate band 'government cannot add on any additional charges, such as cost of mailing or paper'. Electronic transmittal chargeable at actual cost (subd. 3(c) 'electronically transmitting'). In-person inspection/pickup carries no inspection fee (subd. 3(a)).

resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(c); § 13.04, subd. 3
resolutions.source_language: ... the responsible authority may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of searching for and retrieving government data, including the cost of employee time, and for making, certifying, and electronically transmitting the copies of the data or the data ...
resolutions.notes: No fixed certification fee — certifying is an actual-cost component of the copy charge ('making, certifying'); same standard for data subjects under § 13.04 subd. 3 ('actual costs of making and certifying the copies', MN-0010). No separate per-document certification rate found in ch. 13 or the 1205 rules.

resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(c), (e)
resolutions.source_language: If a person requests copies or electronic transmittal of the data to the person, the responsible authority may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of searching for and retrieving government data, including the cost of employee time, and for making, certifying, and electronically transmitting the copies of the data or the data, but may not charge for separating public from not public data.
resolutions.notes: No per-recording, per-minute, or free-minutes schedule exists — audio/video copies fall under the general actual-cost standard (DPO guidance groups 'data stored electronically, photographs, etc.' under actual cost). Redaction of not-public portions of recordings is non-chargeable (subd. 3(c) separation prohibition). No AV-specific fee provision found in ch. 13 (incl. § 13.825 body-worn-camera classification, which sets no fee schedule) or the 1205 rules.

resolutions.value: no commercial-purpose requester surcharge; instead, a data-based fee: copies of commercial-value data developed with significant public expenditure may carry a reasonable fee ADDED to copy costs, capped by demonstrable actual development costs, with a documentation-on-request duty
resolutions.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(d)
resolutions.source_language: When a request under this subdivision involves any person's receipt of copies of public government data that has commercial value and is a substantial and discrete portion of or an entire formula, pattern, compilation, program, device, method, technique, process, database, or system developed with a significant expenditure of public funds by the government entity, the responsible authority may charge a reasonable fee for the information in addition to the costs of making and certifying the copies. Any fee charged must be clearly demonstrated by the government entity to relate to the actual development costs of the information. The responsible authority, upon the request of any person, shall provide sufficient documentation to explain and justify the fee being charged.
resolutions.notes: Minnesota's rule keys on the DATA's commercial value (databases/systems built with significant public funds), not the REQUESTER's commercial purpose — no purpose-based surcharge or labor-becomes-chargeable switch exists. Engine shape: optional add-on fee, ceiling = demonstrable actual development costs, plus a mandatory justify-on-request notice duty.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04 (full text); Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO Copy Costs / Actual Cost guidance
resolutions.notes: The Data Practices Act contains NO fee-waiver provisions — no indigence or public-interest waiver grounds, no purpose statement, no written-denial or waiver-appeal requirement. Because charging is permissive throughout ('may require ... payment'), an entity may simply decline to charge; waiver policy is left to the city. Requesters may not be asked to identify themselves or justify an inspection request, so a purpose-statement waiver test would sit awkwardly with the Act — flag for human review if a city wants one. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04; Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5; DPO guidance
resolutions.notes: No provision forfeits the fee on a late response. Minnesota's response standard itself is non-numeric ('appropriate and prompt manner' / 'as soon as reasonably possible'), so there is no deadline whose breach could trigger forfeiture. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

resolutions.source_authority: Searched: Minn. Stat. §§ 13.03, 13.04 (full text); Minn. R. ch. 1205; DPO guidance
resolutions.notes: No repeat-request carry-forward or fee-aggregation rules found in ch. 13, the 1205 rules, or DPO guidance. The subd. 3(g) suspension (MN-9001) operates per-request and does not aggregate across requests. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

new_rules.legal_concept: Suspension of further response when available data/copies are not inspected or collected and paid for within five business days
new_rules.atomic_rule: If the responsible authority has notified the requester that responsive data or copies are available and the requester does not inspect the data or collect the copies within five business days of the notification, the authority may suspend any further response to the request until the requester inspects the data or collects and pays for the produced copies.
new_rules.trigger: Availability notification sent; requester fails to inspect or collect within 5 business days.
new_rules.clock_spec: pauses: any further response, 5 business-days from availability notification; resumes on inspection or collection-and-payment
new_rules.source_language: If a responsible authority has notified the requesting person that responsive data or copies are available for inspection or collection, and the requesting person does not inspect the data or collect the copies within five business days of the notification, the responsible authority may suspend any further response to the request until the requesting person inspects the data that has been made available, or collects and pays for the copies that have been produced.
new_rules.notes: NEW 2025 provision — the library's known recency gap. Permissive ('may suspend'); consequence is suspension, not withdrawal; cure restores processing. Also the statute's only payment gate: further response may be withheld until produced copies are paid for.

new_rules.legal_concept: Actual costs of making, certifying, and electronically transmitting copies (general copy path)
new_rules.atomic_rule: When copies or electronic transmittal are requested (outside the 100-or-fewer b/w letter/legal page band), the responsible authority may require payment of the actual costs of making, certifying, and electronically transmitting the copies.
new_rules.trigger: Request for copies or electronic transmittal not on the <=100-page b/w flat-rate band.
new_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost (making + certifying + electronic transmission)
new_rules.source_language: If a person requests copies or electronic transmittal of the data to the person, the responsible authority may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of searching for and retrieving government data, including the cost of employee time, and for making, certifying, and electronically transmitting the copies of the data or the data, but may not charge for separating public from not public data.
new_rules.notes: Complements MN-0008 (which carries the search/retrieval half of the same sentence) with the making/certifying/transmitting half. Displaced by the $0.25/page ceiling on the <=100-page b/w band (MN-0009). Refined by delegated rule Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4 (MN-9006).

new_rules.legal_concept: No charge for separating public from not public data (redaction/segregation)
new_rules.atomic_rule: The responsible authority may not charge for separating public from not public data.
new_rules.trigger: Responsive records require redaction/segregation of not-public data before release.
new_rules.source_language: ... but may not charge for separating public from not public data.
new_rules.notes: Makes review/redaction labor categorically non-chargeable statewide. Guidance layer concurs: Advisory Opinion 04-072 (employee time to separate public from not public data excluded; sorting/reviewing/verifying accuracy excluded if not necessary for copying).

new_rules.legal_concept: Additional reasonable fee for copies of commercial-value data developed with significant public expenditure
new_rules.atomic_rule: When a request involves receipt of copies of public data with commercial value that is a substantial/discrete portion or all of a formula, compilation, program, database, or system developed with significant public expenditure, the responsible authority may charge a reasonable fee in addition to copy costs; the fee must be clearly demonstrated to relate to actual development costs, and sufficient justifying documentation must be provided on request.
new_rules.trigger: Request for copies of commercial-value data (substantial/discrete portion of a publicly funded formula, compilation, program, database, or system).
new_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: demonstrable actual development costs of the information (added to copy costs)
new_rules.source_language: When a request under this subdivision involves any person's receipt of copies of public government data that has commercial value and is a substantial and discrete portion of or an entire formula, pattern, compilation, program, device, method, technique, process, database, or system developed with a significant expenditure of public funds by the government entity, the responsible authority may charge a reasonable fee for the information in addition to the costs of making and certifying the copies. Any fee charged must be clearly demonstrated by the government entity to relate to the actual development costs of the information. The responsible authority, upon the request of any person, shall provide sufficient documentation to explain and justify the fee being charged.
new_rules.notes: Data-based, not requester-purpose-based: keys on the DATA's commercial value, not the requester's commercial purpose. Secondary rule type: Requirement (documentation-on-request duty). Fee sits ON TOP of the copy charge.

new_rules.legal_concept: Electronic-form copy of computer-stored data at actual cost; no format conversion required
new_rules.atomic_rule: An entity maintaining public data in a computer storage medium shall provide an electronic-form copy if it can reasonably do so, is not required to provide the data in a different format or program than the one in which it maintains the data, and may require payment of the actual cost of providing the copy.
new_rules.trigger: Request for an electronic copy of public data held in a computer storage medium.
new_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of providing the electronic copy
new_rules.source_language: The responsible authority of a government entity that maintains public government data in a computer storage medium shall provide to any person making a request under this section a copy of any public data contained in that medium, in electronic form, if the government entity can reasonably make the copy or have a copy made. This does not require a government entity to provide the data in an electronic format or program that is different from the format or program in which the data are maintained by the government entity. The entity may require the requesting person to pay the actual cost of providing the copy.
new_rules.notes: Anchors electronic-media and programming/extraction charging at actual cost; the no-conversion-required sentence bounds what programming labor can be demanded. Media cost (USB etc.) includable per DPO guidance (MN-9008).

new_rules.legal_concept: Reasonable-fee factors for copies of public data (delegated rule)
new_rules.atomic_rule: In setting a reasonable fee for copies of public data, the responsible authority shall be guided by: (A) cost of materials including paper; (B) cost of labor to prepare the copies; (C) any schedule of standard copying charges established by the agency in its normal course of operations; (D) special costs necessary to produce copies from machine-based record-keeping systems including computers and microfilm systems; and (E) mailing costs.
new_rules.trigger: Responsible authority determines a fee for providing copies of public data.
new_rules.clock_spec: soft-standard: 'reasonable fee' guided by five enumerated cost factors (no dollar figures)
new_rules.source_language: The responsible authority may charge a reasonable fee for providing copies of public data. In determining the amount of the reasonable fee, the responsible authority shall be guided by the following: A. the cost of materials, including paper, used to provide the copies; B. the cost of the labor required to prepare the copies; C. any schedule of standard copying charges as established by the agency in its normal course of operations; D. any special costs necessary to produce such copies from machine based record keeping systems, including but not limited to computers and microfilm systems; and E. mailing costs.
new_rules.source_authority: Minn. R. 1205.0300, subp. 4 (statutory authority Minn. Stat. § 13.07)
new_rules.notes: Delegated instrument opened per the step-2 mandate (§ 13.07 delegation to the commissioner of administration). Contains NO dollar figures — only the reasonable-fee factor framework. Predates and must be read with the § 13.03 subd. 3(c) 25-cent band and separation prohibition; the statute governs on conflict. Factor C expressly lets the entity use its own standard copying-charge schedule.

new_rules.legal_concept: Data subject: free viewing of private data; reasonable fee for copies (delegated rule)
new_rules.atomic_rule: The responsible authority shall not charge the data subject any fee where the data subject only desires to view private data, and may charge the data subject a reasonable fee for providing copies of private data.
new_rules.trigger: Data subject seeks to view, or requests copies of, private data about themselves.
new_rules.clock_spec: soft-standard: reasonable fee for copies only; viewing free
new_rules.source_language: The responsible authority shall not charge the data subject any fee in those instances where the data subject only desires to view private data. The responsible authority may charge the data subject a reasonable fee for providing copies of private data.
new_rules.source_authority: Minn. R. 1205.0400, subp. 5 (statutory authority Minn. Stat. § 13.07)
new_rules.notes: Second delegated instrument opened. Secondary rule type: Permission (copies fee). Data-subject regime — mirrors § 13.04 subd. 3 (MN-0010: actual costs of making and certifying; no search/retrieval charge to data subjects per DPO guidance). Fee-amount criteria cross-reference part 1205.0300 (MN-9006).

new_rules.legal_concept: Actual-cost components: lowest-paid-capable-employee rate; includable and excluded cost categories (Commissioner advisory-opinion guidance)
new_rules.atomic_rule: In calculating actual cost, employee time must be based on the wages/salary (may include benefits) of the lowest-paid entity employee who could complete the task; includable: media, mailing, copy-preparation time, outside reproduction costs, search/retrieval time (except for data-subject requesters); excluded: separation/redaction time, copier operating expenses, invoice preparation, off-site return, unnecessary sorting/review, sales tax, accounting functions, inspection-related costs.
new_rules.trigger: Entity calculates an actual-cost copy charge.
new_rules.clock_spec: soft-standard: actual cost, employee time at lowest-paid-capable-employee rate
new_rules.source_language: Note: Employee time must be calculated based on the wages/salary (may include benefits) of the lowest-paid entity employee who could complete the task (Advisory Opinion 04-056)
new_rules.source_authority: MN Dept. of Administration, Data Practices Office, 'Actual Cost' page (Advisory Opinions 04-056, 00-054, 95-044, 97-012, 04-072, 01-066, 04-040, 04-055, 94-059, 99-024, 04-003, 04-038)
new_rules.notes: GUIDANCE LAYER, not statute — Commissioner of Administration advisory opinions are persuasive interpretation of § 13.03 subd. 3(c). The atomic rule condenses the page's includable/excluded lists; the quoted clause is verbatim from the opened page. Underlying opinions not individually opened — cite the guidance page, flag opinion-level verification if litigated.

new_rules.legal_concept: 25-cent band glosses: 50 cents two-sided; flat rate with no add-on charges (guidance)
new_rules.atomic_rule: On the 100-or-fewer-page black-and-white letter/legal band, the maximum charge is 25 cents per page or 50 cents for a two-sided copy, as a flat rate to which no additional charges (such as mailing or paper) may be added.
new_rules.trigger: Request on the <=100-page b/w letter/legal paper-copy band.
new_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: $0.25/page single-sided, $0.50 two-sided, flat — no add-ons
new_rules.source_language: For 100 or fewer pages of black and white, letter or legal sized paper copies, the maximum charge allowed is 25 cents for each page copied, or 50 cents for a two-sided copy. This charge is a flat rate; government cannot add on any additional charges, such as cost of mailing or paper.
new_rules.source_authority: MN Dept. of Administration, Data Practices Office, 'Copy Costs' page
new_rules.notes: GUIDANCE LAYER: the 50-cent two-sided figure and the no-add-on 'flat rate' reading appear ONLY on this DPO page, not in § 13.03 subd. 3(c) itself. Statute governs on conflict; treat the glosses as the Commissioner's interpretation. Also states charging is permissive: 'The Data Practices Act allows, but does not require, government to charge for copies.'

delegations_followed.statute_cite: Minn. Stat. § 13.07 (commissioner of administration shall adopt rules to implement ch. 13); cross-referenced by DPO 'Copy Costs' guidance
delegations_followed.instrument: Minnesota Rules, part 1205.0300, subpart 4 — Determining fee for copies (public data)
delegations_followed.figures_extracted: NONE — no dollar figures; 'reasonable fee' guided by five cost factors (materials, labor, agency standard schedule, machine-based special costs, mailing costs)
delegations_followed.applies_to: all_public_bodies (responsible authorities generally; ch. 1205 implements ch. 13, which covers state agencies, statewide systems, and political subdivisions)

delegations_followed.statute_cite: Minn. Stat. § 13.07; cross-referenced by DPO 'Copy Costs' guidance
delegations_followed.instrument: Minnesota Rules, part 1205.0400, subpart 5 — Fees (access to private data)
delegations_followed.figures_extracted: NONE — viewing free for data subjects; 'reasonable fee' permitted for copies of private data, criteria cross-referencing part 1205.0300

applicability_notes: Minn. Stat. ch. 13 applies to every 'government entity' — state agencies, statewide systems, AND political subdivisions — so the § 13.03 fee rules bind municipalities directly; no separate agency-only uniform fee schedule exists in Minnesota.

§ 13.03 subd. 10 (money collected for copies deposited outside the general fund) is expressly limited to 'a responsible authority in a state agency' — state-agency treasury accounting only, no municipal effect; excluded from the resolutions.

Minn. R. ch. 1205 was adopted under § 13.07 to implement ch. 13 and speaks to 'the responsible authority' generally; treated as all_public_bodies. It contains no figures, so nothing turns on the scope call.

The DPO 'Actual Cost' and 'Copy Costs' pages are Commissioner-of-Administration OFFICIAL GUIDANCE (advisory-opinion layer) applicable to all entities subject to ch. 13, including municipalities — but guidance, not law: the 50-cent two-sided figure and the flat-rate/no-add-on gloss have no statutory text behind them.

Data-subject requesters are a distinct fee regime (§ 13.04 subd. 3; Minn. R. 1205.0400 subp. 5): actual costs of making and certifying copies only — no search/retrieval charge, viewing free; the 25-cent band does not apply to data subjects unless it equals actual cost (DPO guidance).
material_negatives: No estimate regime at all: no itemized-estimate threshold, no requester-response window, no revision trigger, no validity period — the only cost-communication duty is the subd. 3(d) justify-on-request documentation duty for commercial-value data fees.

No statutory deposit or prepayment authority for the general public: the only payment gate is post-production (subd. 3(g), 2025 — suspend further response until produced copies are collected and paid for).
No fee-waiver provisions of any kind (grounds, purpose statement, written denial, appeal) — charging is permissive throughout, so waiver is a city policy choice.
No labor thresholds, free-hours allowances, time increments, overhead percentages, minimum fees, de-minimis thresholds, or repeat/aggregation rules.
Review/redaction labor is categorically NON-chargeable ('may not charge for separating public from not public data') — a prohibition, not an absence; several other states charge for this.
No commercial-PURPOSE requester schedule: Minnesota's subd. 3(d) surcharge keys on the data's commercial value, not the requester's purpose.

The delegated rules (Minn. R. 1205.0300 subp. 4, 1205.0400 subp. 5) contain NO dollar figures — only reasonable-fee factors; the only numeric figures in Minnesota fee law are the statutory 25 cents/100 pages and the guidance-only 50 cents two-sided.
gaps_manual_verification: labor.overheadPct: the benefits-includable / overhead-excluded framework rests entirely on the DPO guidance page citing Advisory Opinions 04-056, 01-066, 04-040 — the opinions themselves were not opened; verify at the DPO opinion library before a city relies on including benefits.

rules.deposit.threshold: several state-agency data-practices policies assert payment 'may be required in advance' for large fees; the underlying advisory-opinion authority was not opened, and agency policies are not municipal authority — verify before configuring any prepayment gate beyond subd. 3(g).
MN-9009's 50-cent two-sided figure and flat-rate/no-add-on gloss are guidance-only with no statutory text; if challenged, the statute (25 cents 'for each page copied') governs.
MN-9008's includable/excluded lists condense the DPO page (paraphrase in atomic_rule; the quoted employee-time note is verbatim); opinion-level citations not individually opened.
Minn. R. ch. 1205 scope treated as all_public_bodies (implements ch. 13 generally); no figure turns on this, but confirm if the rule layer is ever load-bearing for a municipal dispute.
